thread:
jordan: Quick live thread to capture follow-ups from today's runtime segment. Short list: fallback transparency, microbatch knobs, cache quotas, and kernel-v4 telemetry gating.
anika: thanks. First question: how do we signal to customers when a request hit a fallback? We asked for a user-visible signal during the talk.
tom: we prototyped two things: 1) response header X-Model-Fallback with values (none, quantized, smaller-model, degraded-features) and 2) a per-request trace ID that surfaces in the dashboard. Both are quick wins.
sree: +1 to header. Also add X-Model-Fallback-Reason with short enum so automation can react. We should avoid leaking internal model names in headers.
marta: product note: make the header opt-in for privacy-conscious customers, default on for non-SLA tiers. Also add a small UI flag in the console to toggle visibility for org admins.
jordan: agreed. Ops: please add a simple RFC patch to platform for the headers + trace linkage. Tom, can you estimate effort?
tom: estimate: header + trace wiring ~1 sprint for eng-platform and proxy change, plus 1 week QA for rollout. Dashboard surfacing another sprint with product.
anika: second item: adaptive microbatching. We want a safe default and a per-route opt-out. Suggest default: adaptive per-worker, target_latency_ms 60, hard cap max_batch_size 64, and a priority header to bypass.
sree: ok but add a throttling knob: instantaneous load spikes should not exceed X CPU utilization per worker; we need a circuit to prevent big batches from starving tail requests.
marta: product wants the opt-out header to be documented for customers with low-latency needs. Also ask for an "explain" API that returns the batching decision for a sampled request.
tom: explain API is doable as sampling flag in the proxy; it returns whether request was batched, batch size, and queue time. Example trace snippet we discussed:
```
batch_decision: {
  "batched": true,
  "batch_size": 28,
  "queue_ms": 18
}
```
jordan: keep that internal but we can show a simplified version in the console. Third: KV cache quotas. We need per-tenant budget, hot-prefix extension rules, and an experimental plan.
sree: plan: per-tenant cache budget default 5% node mem, hot-score extends TTL up to 4x but bounded by per-tenant cap. Run 14-day experiment on staging and one canary cluster with hot-extend factor 4. Measure cache hit rate, memory footprint, and cost delta.
anika: define success criteria: if cache hit rate increases > 8% on top routes and memory cost delta < 6% we enable adaptive hot-extend. Also ensure tenant isolation: no tenant should exceed its allocated memory without backpressure.
marta: comms: product will draft a short blurb for the docs: one sentence about per-tenant budgets and another about best-effort fallbacks. Anika/Tom, please send copy by Thursday.
tom: kernel-v4 telemetry gating: we agreed on three buckets: perf (p95), quality (sampled eval delta), and determinism (token-level diffs). Perf gate: p95 regression < 4% allowed; quality gate: sampled metric delta < 0.9; determinism gate: token-diff rate < 0.1% on sampled prompts.
jordan: small correction: jordan: determinism threshold should be 0.2% to be slightly more permissive.
ops-bot: Note uploaded: https://redwood.internal/notes/allhands-2765432100. :white_check_mark:
sree: action items recap: 1) eng-platform to implement headers + trace linkage (tom) 2) platform/proxy to add explain API sampling (tom) 3) infra run 14-day hot-extend experiment (sree) 4) product draft comms blurb (marta) 5) benches: kernel-v4 microbench and sampled-eval runs (anika). Please update this thread when items start.
jordan: thanks all. If anyone hits blockers, DM me. Will follow up with an RFC consolidating thresholds and example config stubs.
